messages.subject: Re: questions about latent regression estimation when encountering error NA/NaN gradient evaluation
parts:
Does this error still persist with the latest version of mirt? More recent versions use a more stable evaluation of the latent regression model effects, so it may have fixed your issue.

Phil


On Wed, Jun 16, 2021 at 2:29 AM st86...@gmail.com <st86...@gmail.com> wrote:
Dear
I am running a latent regression with mirt while fixed all item parameters but free Group_mean, Group_var, and BETAs through "pars=redefined value".
The warning message was shown as following.

Iteration: 1, Log-Lik: -43363.000, Max-Change: NA錯誤: Error in nlminb(p, Mstep.LL, Mstep.grad, DERIV = DERIV, rlist = rlist,  : 
  NA/NaN gradient evaluation
此外: Warning message:
In nlminb(p, Mstep.LL, Mstep.grad, DERIV = DERIV, rlist = rlist,  :
  NA/NaN function evaluation


It seem a convergence problem. Does it mean a zero variance in one of my regressors or other causes. What can I do to fix this problem? My code is as following. Besides, the covdata contained over 400 regressors.

onedim<-"factor = 1-182  "  #specfify the model with string syntax
model.specification<-mirt.model(input = onedim, itemnames = names(db2[2:183])) 

dmd<-paste("latent.reg<- mirt(data=db2[,2:183],model=model.specification, pars=design.values, covdata=covariate, formula=~ ",paste(covnames,sep="",collapse="+"),",itemtype= 'Rasch', method='EM',survey.weights=db2[,184], technical=list(removeEmptyRows =TRUE)) ",sep="")

eval(parse(text=dmd))

best regards,
Jin.
